lessonTitle: Evidence Claim: Which Event Most Changed Florida?
title: Check My Claim
details: 📅 Q3 · Unit 9 · Synthesis 2: Florida at a Crossroads

badge.name: Field Seal 21
badge.line: Only field historians earn this one. You went where your teacher can't go, and you brought back proof.

hook.look: A field file is a job card. It tells a historian where to go and what to bring back.
hook.head: Field File 21 · Check My Claim
rows: A library, where historians check facts
Your teacher, still stuck inside Canvas
hook.alt: An old color print of soldiers fighting in a pine forest
hook.cap: The Battle of Olustee, 1864, as artists drew it in 1894. State Archives of Florida.
hook.note: I have to decide which event changed Florida the most. Can you go to a library, where historians check facts, and tell me your claim?

opti.brief: She can't leave Canvas, so you go. Visit a library in VR and record your claim in one short video.
opti.desk: No headset? Use my desk. Play the game, then write 2 sentences for your teacher.

vr.h3: Make a Claim in the Library
vr.look: A claim is one sentence that says what you think is true. Evidence is a fact you can check, like a date, a name or a number. Libraries keep records, so historians check facts there.
say: I think ___ changed Florida the most.
One fact that proves it is ___.

steps.title: Get ready
steps.html:
@PLACE@

In your video, you say these 2 sentences:

@SAY@

Practice now. Say both before the timer ends.

@TIMER@

In VR, this page is on the Canvas tab.

steps.title: Go in
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Library in Filter environments. Click National Library, then Begin Solo. Pick your event before you go in: territory (1821), statehood (1845), the Civil War (1861) or Reconstruction (1865).

steps.title: Scout the library
steps.html: Move with the thumbstick. Look at the shelves and the tables. Stop where you can see rows of books.

steps.title: Record your video and send it
steps.html:
Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Fit the shelves in the tablet. Click Record video, say your 2 sentences, and click it again to stop.

On the Canvas tab, pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your video, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 To fix it, send a new video.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your video is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? See Having trouble in VR?

extra.html: Stand in front of the shelves while you record, so your teacher sees where historians check facts.

vr.full: One video, 30 seconds or less, showing the place while you say both sentences.

studio.title: Test the Claims
studio.look: Four claims about Florida. A strong claim passes 3 tests. It names an event and a date. Someone could disagree with it. It has a fact you can check.
studio.do: Tap each test the claim passes. Then tap Check.

game.done: All four tested! Only claims with an event, a date and a fact are strong.

tests.name: Names an event and a date
Has a fact you can check

things.name: Statehood changed Florida.
things.ok: It only passes one test. It is too vague.

things.name: Statehood in 1845 changed Florida the most, because Floridians could now elect their own governor.
things.ok: It passes all three tests. That is a strong claim.

why.argue: Yes, someone could pick another event.
why.fact: Yes: Floridians elected their own governor.

things.name: Secession in 1861 changed Florida the most.
things.ok: Two tests. It needs a fact to back it up.

why.fact: There is no fact here yet.

things.name: Reconstruction changed Florida the most, because in 1871 Josiah T. Walls became Florida's first Black member of Congress.

why.argue: Yes, someone could pick another event.
why.fact: Yes: Walls went to Congress in 1871.

frames.starter: The event that changed Florida the most was ...
One fact that backs it up is ...

studio.full: Your game is done, and your 2 sentences have 20 words or more.
